newsitem.title: NORWAY: Elkem agrees expansion of Icelandic metals plant.
newsitem.headline: Elkem agrees expansion of Icelandic metals plant.

text.p: Norwegian metals producer Elkem ASA said on Thursday it had agreed with the partners in Icelandic Alloys to expand capacity at its ferrosilicon plant on the North Atlantic island by nearly 60 percent.
At the same time, the shareholders have agreed to list Icelandic Alloys on the Icelandic stock exchange, Elkem said.

Shareholders in Icelandic Alloys are the Icelandic state, which holds 55 percent, Elkem with 30 percent and Sumitomo Corp of Japan with 15 percent. Elkem said the Icelandic state would sell some of its stock once the company was listed.
The expansion of the 70,000 tonne per year Grundartangi plant near Reykjavik will entail construction of a third furnace, which will have a capacity of 40,000 tonnes per year.
The new furnace will cost around 250 million Norwegian crowns ($36.8 million) and is due to come into production in 1999.

"Icelandic alloys investments will be financed by an issue of new shares to Elkem ASA, which will give Icelandic Alloys about 90 million (Norwegian) crowns in fresh equity capital," Elkem's statement said.
The issue will increase Elkem's shareholding to 51 percent. ($ = 6.790 Norwegian Crowns)
